You are an Opus build worker on the Fortress revival, working in a git worktree of /home/user/fortress. Read first, in order — your complete context:

1. /home/user/fortress/CLAUDE.md (env exports; FORTRESS_THREADS=1 for ALL runs; component name == filename)
2. explorations/microgpt-iteration2-plan.md — "Standing design rules", "Verified facts", "Correctness anchors", "Worker discipline" bind you (spec-first; never end at first error; no single-data-point rules; no commits, deliverables to scratchpad AND edits in your worktree)
3. explorations/aliases-units-report.md — the research round you are implementing (esp. Q3, probes p14/p15/p16)
4. explorations/microgpt2-diet-report.md — current state of the flagship
5. explorations/microgpt2.fss — the file you will modify (in YOUR worktree only)

BUILD SHORTCUT (do NOT run ant): the main checkout is already built. Copy its build outputs into your worktree before anything else:
  cp -r /home/user/fortress/ProjectFortress/build $PWD/ProjectFortress/
  cp -r /home/user/fortress/default_repository $PWD/ 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p $PWD/default_repository/caches
then export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD (your worktree) and use $PWD/bin/fortress. Never point FORTRESS_HOME at the main checkout (your edited microgpt2 would pollute its caches).

TASK (approved by Pavol): adopt the two named spaces in explorations/microgpt2.fss, with one mandated design probe first.

**Step 0 — MANDATED PROBE (Pavol's caveat, verbatim: "ProbDist cost (Costs 6 lines plus one duplicated overload) — can't this be eliminated by using other features of Fortress type system like traits?").** Before touching microgpt2.fss, probe whether the duplicated `ProbDist × Mat` juxtaposition body can be eliminated by a shared trait: e.g. a small trait (RowLike or similar) that both Vec and ProbDist extend, declaring an abstract accessor (the underlying List) and defining `opr juxtaposition(r: RowLike, m: Mat): Vec` ONCE at trait or top level — precedent: how MultiplicativeRing hands Value its inherited operators (complex_ring precedent, plan file "Verified facts"). Verify it coexists legally with the `Mat × Vec` direction (the Rank1-excludes-Rank2 mechanism, report Q3.2 case 2 / probe p14_named_spaces.fss — start from a copy of explorations/alias-units-probes/p14_named_spaces.fss). Also check: does the shared trait break the `opr =` definitions, `|x|`, subscripting, or generator integration the carriers rely on? Try at least two designs if the first fails (e.g. operator on the trait as a method vs top-level function on the trait type; `comprises` clause or not). If dedup works: adopt it. If not: record every attempt's error verbatim + spec section consulted, classify (implementation gap / design limit), and fall back to the duplicated overload. Either outcome is page content.

**Step 1 — adopt `KVCache`** per report Q3.2 case 1 / probe p16_kvcache.fss: carrier named KVCache; forward signature becomes (Vec, KVCache, KVCache); absorb emptyHist and the two parallel extension comprehensions into an extend operation. Net lines should be ≤ 0; count them.

**Step 2 — adopt `ProbDist`** per Q3.2 case 2 (with Step 0's outcome): softmax : Vec → ProbDist; nll keeps logits: Vec; sample takes ProbDist. The flagship attention line `attend(q,K,V) = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V` must stay VERBATIM.

**Gates (all mandatory, in your worktree):**
- goldenCheck: run the golden config — 15 logits + mean loss 1.228662661701597 + 5 grads at 1e-9 must PASS (correctness anchor in the plan file).
- A short training run (~30 steps) sanity check, FORTRESS_THREADS=1.
- Recount stripped core lines with the diet report's counting instruments (scratchpad …/diet/strip.py, segments.py if still present; else reimplement the same rules) — report the new core total vs 206 vs Python's 152.

**Step 3 — regenerate affected Fortify figures** in explorations/fortify/ (your worktree): any per-block figure whose signature changed (softmax, attention/forward if KVCache appears in a rendered signature) plus sheet-notation if the carrier roster changed. Recipe in any .tic header (fortick → latex → dvisvgm, light+dark SVGs). Check the renders: KVCache and ProbDist should typeset as words (no underscore-bold needed).

**Step 4 — memo** to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/named-spaces/: report.md — Step 0 outcome with every probe verbatim; diffs summary; line accounting (before/after, what KVCache removed, what ProbDist cost with/without dedup); gate outputs; which figures regenerated; any new traps. Copy your probe .fss files there too. Also copy your final microgpt2.fss and changed fortify files there (belt and braces — the coordinator integrates from your worktree, but the worktree may be cleaned).

Do NOT: touch the presentation HTML (coordinator's job), commit, push, or modify anything in the MAIN checkout. Your worktree edits to explorations/microgpt2.fss and explorations/fortify/* are the deliverable. Be thorough; make report.md self-contained.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Use this when users request creating art using code, generative art, algorithmic art, flow fields, or particle systems. Create original algorithmic art rather than copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.

Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. 1	# Fortress revival
2	
3	This is @palimondo's revival of Sun/Oracle's **Fortress** programming language
4	(Guy Steele's HPC language, 2003–2012; interpreter + partial JVM compiler,
5	BSD-licensed). The repo carries the full available git history (5397 commits,
6	root 2007-01-04, HEAD Aug 2012) with pluckyporcupine's Scala 2.10.7/Java 9
7	migration grafted on top as a tree overlay — see the commit messages of the
8	graft commits for lineage and attribution. Working mode: Claude explains the
9	codebase and produces documentation and experiments as we go; Pavol decides
10	what gets committed. The full collaboration protocol — roles, tone, how work
11	is presented, commit discipline, delegation — is in
12	`explorations/protocol.md`; read it at session start.
13	
14	## Build and run (verified: Ubuntu 24.04 container, JDK 25 — current rung)
15	
16	```bash
17	apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant  # JDK 8/11/17/21 also still work (all gated green)
18	export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
19	export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
20	export FORTRESS_HOME=<repo root>
21	unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS                          # proxy trust-store options confuse ant's JVM forks
22	cd $FORTRESS_HOME && ant compileAll              # ~80 s
23	./bin/fortress explorations/claude_demo.fss      # interpreter ("walk") — this works
24	```
25	
26	Toolchain (2026-08-21): Scala 2.13.18 (build.xml drives scalac via
27	`scala.tools.nsc.Main` directly — Scala 2.13 dropped the `scala.tools.ant`
28	tasks), ASM 9.10.1 (vendored in
29	`ProjectFortress/third_party/asm/`; watch out — Fortress's own
30	`asmbytecodeoptimizer.Opcodes` shadows `org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes` in that
31	package), `-source/-target 1.8` and emitted classfiles V1_6 (both now
32	merely conventions — ASM 9 unblocks raising them as a deliberate later
33	step), sources compiled as UTF-8 (all sources were already valid UTF-8;
34	the old ISO-8859-1 javac attributes just mis-decoded comments),
35	work-stealing runtime on stdlib `java.util.concurrent` ForkJoin (vendored
36	jsr166y retired); see `explorations/modernization-plan.md` for the ladder
37	and current rung.
38	
39	Facts that save time:
40	
41	- **Both execution paths work.** `fortress <file>.fss` interprets directly.
42	  The bytecode compiler path (`fortress compile` + `fortress run`) also works
43	  on JDK 8 — pluckyporcupine's "compiled programs don't run" is wrong here —
44	  but has two traps: imported library components (`System`,
45	  `CompilerSystem`) must be explicitly `fortress compile`d into the cache
46	  first, and **stale caches** cause a misleading
47	  `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)` — wipe
48	  `default_repository/caches/*` and recompile in library order (recipe in
49	  `explorations/repo-internals.md`). The compiler is incomplete (some
50	  constructs still `sayWhat`), not broken. See
51	  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
52	- **`ProjectFortress/hello.fss` runs only via the compiler path** — its July
53	  2012 upgrade imports `System.getProperty`/`CompilerSystem.args`, which the
54	  interpreter can't resolve. Use `explorations/*.fss` as interpreter smoke
55	  tests.
56	- **Test suite (2026-08-19): fully green.** `ant testFast` (~1,400 tests
57	  incl. the full compiler suite) and `ant testSystem` (382 interpreter
58	  tests) both pass with zero failures — the first fully green suite in this
59	  lineage (the 2012 mainline ended with 7 red). History and the two fixes:
60	  `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
61	- The interpreter requires filename (sans `.fss`) == component name.
62	- If scalac fails with arity errors in `S*Pattern` nodes, the generated AST
63	  sources are stale relative to `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`:
64	  `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast && ant compileAll` regenerates.
65	- Interpreter caches live in `default_repository/caches/` (gitignored); wipe
66	  them if library edits seem to have no effect.
67	- Architecture map, name-resolution rules, cache anatomy, test-harness
68	  mechanics, and git-archaeology techniques: `explorations/repo-internals.md`
69	  — read it before diving into the source.
70	
71	## Layout
72	
73	- Original Fortress tree: everything not listed below — do not modify
74	  casually; it is the historical artifact being revived.
75	- `explorations/` — revival-era experiments and writeups (ours; verified
76	  running programs).
77	- `research/` — the Guy Steele corpus: `research/README.md` is a committed
78	  links-only index; `research/extracts/` holds committed working notes;
79	  `research/decks/` is **gitignored** (copyrighted PDFs, dropped in per
80	  session, never committed).
81	- `Specification/` + `Specification-1.0-frozen/` — the language spec LaTeX
82	  (in-repo, richer than the published PDF; building it is untested).
83	
84	## Project goals (rough order)
85	
86	1. ~~Baseline the 2012 test suite~~ DONE — fully green on JDK 8 (see above).
87	2. Modernization ladder — **approved plan, standing orders, and current rung:
88	   `explorations/modernization-plan.md`** (Scala 2.12 ✓ → JDK 11 → UTF-8 →
89	   jsr166y→j.u.c. → JDK 17/21 → ASM 9 → Scala 2.13 eval; each rung gated on
90	   the fully green suite; CI early).
91	3. Complex numbers: the spec promises ℂ but zero complex arithmetic shipped;
92	   seed is `explorations/complex_ring.fss`.
93	4. Fix the bytecode compiler path — characterized 2026-08-24: the gap is
94	   the compiler's tiny prelude library, not codegen; prioritized worklist
95	   and measured 6.8–8.9× payoff in `explorations/compiled-path-gaps.md`.
96	5. Grow the Steele research corpus (`research/README.md` lists open hunts).
97	6. microgpt.fss — port Karpathy's 243-line dependency-free GPT (scalar
98	   autodiff, char-level transformer) to interpreter Fortress as an
99	   executable-paper showcase; feasibility map and staging:
100	   `explorations/microgpt-port.md`.
101	
102	Claims in old READMEs (root `README.txt`, pluckyporcupine's `README.md`,
103	`NOTES.md`) describe *their* eras, not the current tree — verify against the
104	code before acting on them.

1	# microgpt iteration 2: plan for the from-scratch notation exploration
2	
3	Approved by Pavol 2026-08-26. This file is the complete context for every
4	worker in the run. Read it fully before doing anything.
5	
6	## Mission (approved verbatim in essence)
7	
8	Test Fortress's founding claim on the best possible specimen. The claim:
9	the gap between how ML literature states a transformer's mathematics and
10	how programs implement it is a language defect that Fortress was built
11	to close. The specimen: Karpathy's microgpt, the smallest complete GPT.
12	The test: construct, in running and verified Fortress, the notation that
13	lets each building block of the model be stated so that its typeset form
14	and the literature's own formula sit side by side and the reader can
15	judge the distance **by eye**. The deliverable teaches two things at
16	once and inseparably: how a GPT works (a reader starting from zero
17	leaves understanding it) and how the notation is constructed (what the
18	language gives, what it must be taught, and what it cannot yet say).
19	Where the correspondence fails, the failure is shown and classified —
20	implementation gap (revival worklist) versus design limit. Everything
21	shown runs; correctness is anchored to the Python reference; the
22	process is documented.
23	
24	**Not the mission** (named local minima — do not fall into them):
25	fidelity to Steele's 2015 slide idioms; preservation of any prior
26	rung's code structure (this iteration starts FROM SCRATCH); the golden
27	check as an aesthetic constraint (it is a correctness instrument only);
28	interpreter speed (measured, reported, never steering notation).
29	
30	## Standing design rules (from Pavol, binding)
31	
32	1. **No custom BIG operators** (`BIG OPLUS`, `BIG BOXPLUS`, any new
33	   glyph) unless the form is (a) genuinely the prevalent way ML
34	   literature writes that mathematics, or (b) provably the only working
35	   way in current Fortress, with the spec-vs-implementation gap
36	   documented. The ML literature writes Σ, Π, 𝔼, max — never custom big
37	   operators. Glyph imitation of Σ is not Σ. Default: named functions
38	   (`sum(...)`) over comprehensions; the genuine library `SUM` where
39	   summands are `Number`s (e.g. over `.data` inside a sum-node
40	   constructor).
41	2. **The specification is the first authority** for any language
42	   question: `Specification/` LaTeX sources (byte-identical to
43	   1.0-frozen in all chapters audited so far). Order of authority:
44	   spec → `explorations/expressiveness-review.md` (audited findings
45	   with probes) → library sources → fresh empirical probe. Never end a
46	   design path at the first interpreter error: check what the spec
47	   sanctions (the vector×matrix "impossibility" had a documented
48	   escape, the Meet Rule / `excludes`), then record divergence.
49	3. **No single-data-point rules.** Any claimed constraint ("always
50	   parenthesize X", "Y is impossible") requires either a spec citation
51	   or two independent probes, recorded.
52	
53	## Verified facts (do not re-derive; probes in `explorations/spec-probes/`)
54	
55	- List/comprehension element-type ascriptions `[\T\]` are needed ONLY
56	  when elements' runtime class differs from the target (numeric
57	  literals → `FloatLiteral`; nested `ArrayList[\…\]` under invariant
58	  `List`). For concrete object element types (like an autodiff node)
59	  they are redundant. Return types on definitions are optional
60	  (inference chapter in the spec is a stub; the implementation infers).
61	  The `zip` static argument is mandatory.
62	- The algebraic tower that exists: `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and
63	  `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` only (`FortressLibrary.fss:328,340`).
64	  Extending `MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` with `one`/`TIMES` inherits
65	  juxtaposition, binary minus, `zero` (precedent:
66	  `explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The spec's full
67	  `Monoid…Field` chapter ships only as commented-out
68	  `Library/incomplete/…INCOMPLETE`.
69	- Two juxtaposition (or any operator) overloads on `(List,List)` shapes
70	  are illegal — but **mutually excluding carrier traits make both
71	  directions legal** (library's own Vector/Matrix at
72	  `FortressLibrary.fss:2634,2641` via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; probes
73	  `p7_excludes.fss`, `p14_genwrap.fss` — a six-line carrier object also
74	  buys `|x|`, `x[i]`, `x[r]`, generator integration, `.map`, clean
75	  renders).
76	- `SUM` is closed to user types three ways (library `Number` seal,
77	  spec's no-static-param-overloading rule, desugarer's one-nullary-
78	  registration-per-name). Coercion parses but is unwired. Multifix
79	  dispatch is unimplemented. `Number` already has `SQRT`.
80	- Real parse traps (verified): chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`
81	  (grammatical by design, `concrete-syntax.tex:921`); `^` after a call
82	  or dotted field needs parens; `|w||>` and `/|` need a space; `V`
83	  cannot name a variable while object `V` is in scope. FALSIFIED trap,
84	  do not propagate: "comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need
85	  parens" — they don't.
86	- Interpreter performance law: run everything `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`
87	  (idle-worker micro-forking makes 2 workers slower than 1).
88	- `nat`-parameterized user vectors with dimension-checked ops run
89	  (`p9_natvec.fss`) — available as a design ingredient, not a mandate.
90	
91	## Correctness anchors
92	
93	- The golden check: deterministic-weight config in
94	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` `goldenCheck()` — 15 logits + mean loss
95	  1.228662661701597 + 5 gradients at 1e-9. Any complete candidate must
96	  pass it (values are architecture-level truths, independent of
97	  notation). Nucleus-stage candidates use the lighter analytic checks
98	  (style of `explorations/mgnative_a.fss` run()) or hand-computed
99	  attention values.
100	- Reference implementations for BEHAVIOR only (not style):
101	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` (v1), `microgpt_native.fss`,
102	  `microgpt_paper.fss`. Architecture facts: 1 layer, heads structural,
103	  rmsnorm without gain, no biases, plain relu, causal by history,
104	  Adam β₁ .85 β₂ .99 lr .01 linear decay, BOS=26 vocab 27.
105	
106	## Fitness function
107	
108	For each building block, typeset the Fortress definition with Fortify
109	(recipe in any `explorations/fortify/*.tic` header: fortick → latex →
110	dvisvgm; rasterize with chromium `--headless --no-sandbox --screenshot`)
111	and hold it against the literature's formula for that block:
112	
113	- h⁰ = Wₑ[t] + Wₚ[i]
114	- RMSNorm(x) = x / √(x·x/d + ε)
115	- A(q,kⱼ) = q·kⱼ/√d_k ; weights = softmax over j≤i ; out = Σⱼ pⱼvⱼ
116	  (vector form: softmax(qKᵀ/√d_k)V)
117	- FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁ x)
118	- L = −log softmax(logits)_y
119	- Adam: element-wise update equations (index form IS the literature here)
120	
121	Judged by eye: would a reader of the paper recognize the line? Every
122	departure needs a reason from the classification {implementation gap,
123	design limit, deliberate-with-reason}.
124	
125	## Deliverables ladder (this workflow: nucleus stage)
126	
127	Each design candidate delivers a NUCLEUS, not the full model: the
128	notation layer it proposes plus running, checked implementations of
129	rmsnorm, softmax, one-head attention (score+weights+blend over a
130	history), and ffn, over the candidate's own autodiff value type (a
131	minimal tape engine is fine; reuse of engine A's *concepts* is allowed,
132	code written fresh). Plus: its Fortify render sheet, a rasterized PNG,
133	and a design memo (what the language gave / had to be taught / can't
134	say; every deviation classified; what the full model would look like —
135	sketch the forward pass in the candidate's notation).
136	
137	Full-model implementation, presentation build, and integration happen
138	AFTER Pavol-side judgment of the candidates — not in this workflow.
139	
140	## Presentation (context for memos; built after judgment)
141	
142	The rebuilt page interleaves tightly: short concept prose per block,
143	then immediately the paired lines — the literature's formula and the
144	Fortress definition's render, adjacent, no repetition of the formula in
145	prose, no tan "the paper writes" echo boxes, never a big code block
146	followed by explanation. New content queued: the honest-loss-curve
147	section (explorations/training-dynamics.md + chart) and the
148	PRNG/SplitMix lineage note (Fortress's parallelism → Steele's 2014
149	splittable PRNGs; explorations/prng-findings.md). The three prior rungs
150	(transliteration → index → carriers) remain the notation-ladder
151	exhibit.
152	
153	## Worker discipline
154	
155	Worktree only; `ant compileAll` once (env per CLAUDE.md: JDK 25
156	exports, unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD); no commits, no
157	pushes, no tracked-file modifications; deliverables copied to the
158	session scratchpad under your candidate's name; timings indicative
159	(shared box). Report every dead end with the error verbatim and the
160	spec section consulted.
161	
162	## Judgment (2026-08-26, coordinating session; full brief: candidates-decision-brief.md in session scratchpad, mirrored below in spirit)
163	
164	The model notation is the **carriers ⊕ tower merge**; spartan survives as
165	the page's measurement exhibit (its verified price list of what each line
166	of machinery buys). Decisions on the brief's open questions:
167	
168	1. Axis weighting: fidelity and machinery-as-content together — the merge
169	   with tower's inheritance-ledger narrative serves both mission halves.
170	2. Weights typeset **bold** (`_W1` → 𝐖₁): bold-matrix is a genuine,
171	   prevalent ML register; italic-capital subscripts are unreachable
172	   (spec numeral rule + Fortify roman rule — classified design/toolchain
173	   limit, stated on the page).
174	3. **Adopt `^T`**: the flagship attention line becomes the literature's
175	   own `softmax(q Kᵀ/√d_k) V`; the one-line transpose operator is itself
176	   a teachable exhibit.
177	4. **Keep the visible max-shift**, in tower's form: `StandardMax[\V\]`
178	   opens the genuine library `BIG MAX` (no `.data` leak) — an honest
179	   numerics point Karpathy also keeps, and the counterpoint to sealed Σ.
180	5. **Bind `d = |x|` / use `d_k` fields** so the paper's symbols survive
181	   and `|·|` is never misread as a norm.
182	6. Spartan's price list and falsified-trap hygiene become page content.
183	7. Per-head plumbing stays as comprehensions — the literature's
184	   `head₁…head_h` ellipsis made precise, not hidden behind machinery.
185	8. Render sheets show the machinery (carriers, lifts, extends-clauses
186	   framed as the inheritance ledger; `sum()`'s body framed as the
187	   autodiff-sees-Σ lesson) — the mission's second half is not curated
188	   away.
189	9. Mandated cleanups: define carrier `=` (the reflexive-false landmine);
190	   apply all judge reclassifications (carriers D2/D5, tower's `Vv` and
191	   "library fiat"); engine node named `Value` freeing the letter `V`;
192	   the loose-vs-tight-slash footnote; every full-model claim gated on
193	   the golden check.
194	
195	Build target: `explorations/microgpt2.fss`, plus per-block render
196	figures (one small .tic/.svg per block) for the interleaved page.
